newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac says state should not run industry.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac says state should not run industry.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac said on Monday that the French state should not run businesses in the commercial sector and warned the left-wing government it would shut the door to foreign alliances if it kept control.

"The state today no longer has any place in the management of competitive industries," Chirac said in a live television interview. "Today our big companies can't live without alliances and especially European alliances...and modern countries can't imagine their private companies teaming up with public companies subject to conditions that have nothing to do with the market."

He was responding to a question about Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's decision last Friday to halt the privatisation of defence electronics giant Thomson-CSF and keep a "decisive state shareholding" in the firm.

While the conservative Chirac did not mention Thomson by name, his comment about the need for alliances was a clear reference to the company, which the centre-right government defeated on June 1 had planned to sell either to Lagardere Groupe or Alcatel Alsthom.
To preserve French interests, such companies needed European alliances to compete with the giant American and Japanese conglomerates, he said.
The state should restrict its role to creating conditions of economic freedom and ensuring that those who took advantage of them did not abuse their position, the president added.
